Sensitivity Analysis for Sample Size Planning From the AIPE Perspective for Cliff's Delta

Source: R/ss_aipe_cliff_delta_sensitivity.R
ss_aipe_cliff_delta_sensitivity.Rd

Quantifies how much misspecification of the population Cliff's delta (\(\delta = \Pr(X > Y) - \Pr(X < Y)\)) distorts an AIPE-based sample size plan. On each replication the function simulates two independent samples whose population Cliff's delta equals true_delta, computes the sample cliff_delta and its CI, and summarizes the realized widths and coverage.

Replications without an interval. When the two simulated groups are completely separated (every score of one above every score of the other), or every score is equal, the estimated variance of Cliff's delta is 0 and cliff_delta reports both limits equal to the estimate, with a warning that they are not a confidence interval. Such a replication has no interval here. Its estimate still enters mean_cliff_delta, median_cliff_delta, and sd_cliff_delta. The width, width-target, and coverage rows (mean_ci_width, median_ci_width, sd_ci_width, pct_ci_less_width, pct_ci_miss_low, pct_ci_miss_high, total_type_I_error) describe the replications that have an interval, and are NA when none has; pct_ci_less_width is the number of intervals no wider than width divided by the number of replications with an interval. The warning of each replication is not passed on. One warning of class dmar_replications_without_interval, with the fields n_without_interval and G, states how many there were, and the simulation attribute records the counts. Separation is common when true_delta is large in absolute value and the groups are small: with true_delta = 0.9 and six per group, about four replications in ten are separated.

Data generating mechanism. The simulator draws each sample from a normal distribution and chooses the mean shift so that the implied Cliff's delta equals true_delta. For normal samples \(\delta = 2 \Phi(\Delta/\sqrt{2}) - 1\) where \(\Delta\) is the standardized mean difference, so the simulator sets \(\Delta = \sqrt{2} \cdot \Phi^{-1}((1 + \delta)/2)\).

Usage

ss_aipe_cliff_delta_sensitivity(
  true_delta = NULL,
  supposed_delta = NULL,
  ratio = 1,
  width,
  specified_N = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  assurance = NULL,
  G = 1000,
  print_iter = FALSE,
  filename = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

true_delta

Population Cliff's delta (the data generating value); in \((-1, 1)\).

supposed_delta

The supposed population Cliff's delta, the planning value passed to ss_aipe_cliff_delta (not an estimate computed from data); supply this or specified_N but not both.

ratio

Allocation ratio \(n_1 / n_2\) (default 1).

width

Desired full width of the CI on Cliff's delta.

specified_N

Total sample size to evaluate (split per ratio).

conf_level

Confidence level (default 0.95).

assurance

Optional assurance probability.

G

Number of Monte Carlo replications.

print_iter

Logical.

filename

Optional path for a comma separated file recording every replication (the sample Cliff's delta, the two confidence limits, the interval width, and two indicators of whether the interval missed true_delta below or above): nothing is written when filename is NULL (the default), a new file with a header row is created otherwise, an existing file at that path is appended to, and a throwaway run should point it at tempfile(fileext = ".csv"). A replication without an interval is recorded with its estimate and with NA in the other columns.

seed

Optional integer seed. The default NULL draws from, and advances, the current random number stream; an integer makes the call reproducible, and the caller's random number state is restored when the call returns.

Value

A data.frame (class dmar_tbl) with columns term and value and these rows: mean_cliff_delta, median_cliff_delta, and sd_cliff_delta (summaries of the G estimates); mean_ci_width, median_ci_width, and sd_ci_width (summaries of the widths of the replications with an interval); pct_ci_less_width (the proportion of all G replications whose interval is no wider than width); pct_ci_miss_low, pct_ci_miss_high, and total_type_I_error (among the replications with an interval, the proportions whose interval lies wholly above true_delta, wholly below it, and either); n_1, n_2, and total_N (the sample sizes simulated); and the inputs true_delta, supposed_delta (NA when specified_N was given), ratio, width, conf_level, and assurance (present only when an assurance was supplied). The simulation attribute records the numbers of replications attempted, with an interval, and without one (see the section on the record of the simulation).

The record of the simulation

Every sensitivity function of the package summarizes its replications over one denominator: the replications that produced a confidence interval (for a power sensitivity function, a test). The proportion of intervals that met the width target (pct_ci_less_width), the proportions of intervals that missed the true value, and the summaries of the widths are all taken over those replications. A replication without an interval is in none of these rows. It is counted, and the returned table carries the counts in its attribute simulation, a list read with attr(x, "simulation"):

attempted

the number of replications asked for (G).

returned

the number that produced an interval (a test).

failed

the number that did not (attempted - returned).

denominator

the number of replications the rows named above are taken over, which is returned.

width_target_probability

the proportion of the replications with an interval whose interval met the width target, the value of the pct_ci_less_width row; NA for a function or a call without a width target, and when no replication produced an interval.

width_target_mc_ci

the exact binomial (Clopper-Pearson) limits for that proportion, at the confidence level of the table. They describe the error of the simulation, which shrinks as G grows, and nothing else.

A function that records more about its run adds elements to the list, and its help page names them. The line "Replications" beneath the printed table gives G, and the three counts when a replication was without an interval. With many replications without an interval the rows describe only the studies in which the interval could be formed, so failed is to be reported beside them.

References

Cliff, N. (1993). Dominance statistics: Ordinal analyses to answer ordinal questions. Psychological Bulletin, 114(3), 494–509. doi:10.1037/0033-2909.114.3.494

Feng, D., & Cliff, N. (2004). Monte Carlo evaluation of ordinal d with improved confidence interval. Journal of Modern Applied Statistical Methods, 3(2), 322–332. doi:10.22237/jmasm/1099267560

Maxwell, S. E., Delaney, H. D., & Kelley, K. (2027). Designing experiments and analyzing data: A model comparison perspective (4th ed.). Routledge.

Examples

# Small G keeps the Monte Carlo sweep fast; raise G for a real plan.
ss_aipe_cliff_delta_sensitivity(
  true_delta = 0.30, supposed_delta = 0.30,
  width = 0.30, G = 25, print_iter = FALSE, seed = 113
)
#>  term               value
#>  mean_cliff_delta   0.310
#>  median_cliff_delta 0.303
#>  sd_cliff_delta     0.068
#>  mean_ci_width      0.240
#>  median_ci_width    0.241
#>  sd_ci_width        0.008
#>  pct_ci_less_width  1.000
#>  pct_ci_miss_low    0.080
#>  pct_ci_miss_high   0.000
#>  total_type_I_error 0.080
#>  n_1                156  
#>  n_2                156  
#>  total_N            312  
#>  true_delta         0.300
#>  supposed_delta     0.300
#>  ratio              1    
#>  width              0.300
#>  conf_level         0.950
#> 
#> Replications: 25
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%

# A large effect with six per group: some replications are completely
# separated and have no interval. The width and coverage rows describe
# the others, and one warning says how many were without an interval.
ss_aipe_cliff_delta_sensitivity(
  true_delta = 0.90, specified_N = 12, width = 0.40, G = 100,
  seed = 113
)
#> Warning: 43 of 100 replications had completely separated groups (or no variation), where the estimated variance of Cliff's delta is 0 and no confidence interval exists. The width, width-target, and coverage rows describe the other 57 replications.
#>  term               value
#>  mean_cliff_delta   0.914
#>  median_cliff_delta 0.944
#>  sd_cliff_delta     0.103
#>  mean_ci_width      0.959
#>  median_ci_width    0.909
#>  sd_ci_width        0.100
#>  pct_ci_less_width  0.000
#>  pct_ci_miss_low    0.000
#>  pct_ci_miss_high   0.000
#>  total_type_I_error 0.000
#>  n_1                6    
#>  n_2                6    
#>  total_N            12   
#>  true_delta         0.900
#>  supposed_delta     <NA> 
#>  ratio              1    
#>  width              0.400
#>  conf_level         0.950
#> 
#> Replications: 100 attempted, 57 with an interval, 43 without
